name: commit-with-care
trigger: Use when committing work, a branch has become one blob before merging, or history will ever need bisecting.

name: coordinate-the-disclosure
trigger: Use when a vulnerability report arrives, you find a flaw serious enough to disclose yourself, or an embargo clock is running.

name: cut-thin-slices
trigger: Use when implementation begins on anything bigger than a one-liner, or when work spans multiple layers or files.

name: decide-with-records
trigger: Use when choosing technologies, architectures, data shapes, or any decision future builders must know was deliberate.

name: design-the-interface
trigger: Use when an API, public function set, module boundary, plugin surface, or CLI contract is born or extended.

name: document-the-why
trigger: Use when onboarding docs are stale, a decision needs to outlive the decision-maker, or the next reader needs more than the code says.

name: estimate-with-ranges
trigger: Use when anyone asks how long, how much, or whether it fits.

name: fire-a-skill
trigger: Use when a craft is missing from the library and keeps being improvised.

name: ground-truth
trigger: Use when working in an unfamiliar codebase, using a library whose version may differ from training knowledge, or building on any claim you have not personally verified.

name: guide-the-reader
trigger: Use when a user must learn the thing you built, the same question keeps getting answered in chat, or the docs mix teaching with reference into mush.

name: harden-the-edges
trigger: Use when work faces real users, real data, or real attackers: before launch, before handling others' data, before exposing any new endpoint or surface."

name: hunt-the-bug
trigger: Use when behavior is wrong and the cause is unknown, an error keeps resurfacing, or a fix "didn't take".

name: make-it-accessible
trigger: Use when building or changing anything a human will see, hear, or click.

name: measure-then-optimize
trigger: Use when anything is slow and a fix is being proposed, guessed, or defended without numbers.

name: migrate-gently
trigger: Use when a schema, model, stored format, or published interface must change while the system keeps running.

name: model-the-data
trigger: Use when persistent state, schemas, core domain objects, or state machines take shape.

name: observe-the-system
trigger: Use when a service, queue, or long-running process is being built, someone debugs by print-statement, or an incident review says "we had no way to know".

name: open-the-gates
trigger: Use when a release is going out to real users, or when "just deploying this real quick" is being said.

name: question-first
trigger: Use when a request has no acceptance criteria, could mean several materially different things, or the user says "build me X" without constraints.

name: read-the-codebase
trigger: Use when work starts in a repository you do not know, or answers keep citing code nobody has opened.

name: refactor-with-care
trigger: Use when cleaning up code that works, renaming for clarity, or untangling structure - without any intended behavior change.

name: rehearse-the-failure
trigger: Use when the system is about to face reality - a launch, a migration, a high-stakes weekend - and the rollback plan has never been executed.

name: review-the-work
trigger: Use when work is about to be presented as complete, a milestone is claimed, or a change is about to be merged.

name: run-the-postmortem
trigger: Use when an incident is over or contained, a near-miss rattled the team, or the same incident keeps coming back.

name: tend-the-dependencies
trigger: Use when updates are pending, a lockfile drifts, or a major bump is being pushed through in a hurry.

name: test-first
trigger: Use when writing logic that must not break - business rules, parsers, state machines, bug fixes - and when a behavior change needs a permanent guard.

name: test-the-contract
trigger: Use when an interface is published to consumers outside your test suite, or a boundary change is about to ship.

name: test-the-edges
trigger: Use when a suite is green but trust is low, or inputs arrive from outside your control.

name: write-the-spec
trigger: Use when an agreed idea is about to become implementation, a project or significant feature is starting, or requirements exist only in conversation.
